# Performance: the rewrite against C

Release builds, measured 2026-11-11T12:10:18Z to 2026-11-11T12:32:34Z on a 24-CPU x86_64 bare-metal machine (kernel 7.2.9-201.fc44.x86_64), on its fastest CPUs alone (0, 1, 2, 3, 12, 13, 14, 15), the legs' samples interleaved; load average 0.80 before and 2.17 after. The rewrite at `919eed1064ac`. Figures are medians; compare only builds measured on this machine, in one run of this script.

```
c: curl 8.23.1-DEV (Linux) libcurl/8.23.1-DEV OpenSSL/3.5.9 zlib/1.3.1.zlib-ng brotli/1.2.0 zstd/1.5.7 c-ares/1.34.8 libidn2/2.3.8 libpsl/0.21.5 libssh2/1.11.1 nghttp2/1.68.0 ngtcp2/1.25.0 nghttp3/1.18.0 mit-krb5/1.22.2 OpenLDAP/2.6.15

```

Both legs link one HTTP/3 build: ngtcp2 1.25.0 pic gnutls+wolfssl wolfssl-5.9.4 (inventory/measure/deps.py: `configure --disable-dependency-tracking --enable-lib-only --with-openssl --with-gnutls --with-wolfssl --with-pic`) from `build/deps/ngtcp2`, the C legs its shared libraries and the Rust legs its static archives; nghttp3 1.18.0 (`/usr/lib64/libnghttp3.so.9.9.0`).

## scorecard

A run the scorecard reports errors for is left out of its cell's median and counted as failed in it. A requests run fails when a response is not a 200 or the tool exits with an error; with `--parallel`, Rust's tool exits with a transfer's failure where C's can forget it (DIVERGENCE.md), so a run in which both legs lost transfers can fail on the Rust leg alone.
